name: Neon Afterimage
image_style: A striking 16:10 landscape wallpaper in late-1990s CD-ROM cover art fused with airbrushed album illustration, soft analog video bloom, subtle CRT phosphor texture, photocopied grain, and translucent spectral equalizer bands treated as abstract light rather than interface graphics. The mood is nocturnal, nostalgic, playful, and faintly archaeological—like discovering a forgotten music workstation in a quiet museum after closing. Use deep blue-black, smoked violet, electric cyan, oxidized silver, and restrained magenta-red accents; keep highlights luminous but never neon-heavy, with broad low-detail space along the upper edge and a calm darker region for widgets. No lettering, logos, watermarks, borders, frames, or UI.
scene: Exactly one striking 16:10 landscape desktop wallpaper, preferably 2560x1600, set inside a late-1990s municipal media archive at midnight: carpeted acoustic walls, beige rack equipment, a glass-fronted CD carousel, coiled patch cables, a chunky CRT monitor showing only abstract bands of light with no readable interface, and rain-glossed windows overlooking a sleeping city. In the lower-right, Space Ghost is unmistakable in his muscular white costume, black hood and mask, yellow cape, and red power bands, seated rigidly at a mixing desk while carefully cueing a single compact disc with enormous gloved fingers. His cape is draped safely over a spare chair, and a weary archivist continues cataloguing unlabeled discs nearby with restrained bewilderment. The visual joke is his absolute seriousness as an audio engineer in a world of obsolete equipment. Keep the upper third quiet and dark for the desktop panel, with a calm shadowed lower-left area for widgets. No sacred figures, devotional attributes, worship, lettering, logos, watermark, frame, or interface elements.
source_phrase: Something to remind me deeply of the winamp days
